request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Use fold-level evidence to decide: a config that wins a majority of folds is more trustworthy than one with a higher mean but inconsistent fold performance. Between two configs with similar fold-win rates, prefer the simpler model. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 2 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means one config clearly wins most folds and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means fold wins are split roughly evenly or something looks off. You can inspect the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown of any completed run. Compare fold-by-fold: count how many folds each config wins to assess which is genuinely better vs lucky. (Independent run 1.)

concerns: Run 2 wins 4 of 5 folds against run 1 and 4 of 5 against run 3. Run 3 beats it only on fold 4 (0.79 vs 0.7765), and the margin is small.
The mean gain over the random forest is about 0.028 PR-AUC, which is only about half of the fold SD (0.056-0.065). The folds are correlated, so the lead is consistent but modest.
Only 3 configs have been tried, and no simple baseline such as logistic regression has been run. It is unclear whether the gap comes from the model or the feature set.

The PotentialFraud labels have an undocumented origin. They may be rule-based or derived from the same claim features, so high PR-AUC (about 0.73) and ROC-AUC (about 0.945) may reflect label leakage or circularity rather than real fraud detection.
The 'agent' feature set is only partly explained, and it could encode label-related artifacts. Run 2 uses all+agent while run 1 uses all, so model and features are confounded.
Fold 3 is weak for every config (about 0.60-0.65), which suggests a temporal or distribution shift across the 2009 claim window. Check whether the folds are time-aware.
Precision@50 of about 0.78 is the closest proxy for the roughly 100-provider audit queue. It was measured at k=50, not k=100, so queue-level performance is unverified.
Run 3 used class_weight with a smaller model and did worse on average. Imbalance handling does not appear to help here, but the confound with feature_set remains.

next_experiments.rationale: Ablate the agent features while keeping run 2's hyperparameters, to see whether the gain comes from the agent features or from the model. This also checks for leakage.
Add a simple, interpretable baseline. If it comes close to LightGBM on fold-level PR-AUC, the simpler model should be preferred.
